title: What can you say about L-glutamine in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 4 wordings for L-glutamine; the strongest is "Helps restore blood glutamine levels that drop after hard physical stress, such as long, exhausting exercise" (moderate, 5-9 g a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Heals IBS, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis".

supported_wordings.wording: Helps restore blood glutamine levels that drop after hard physical stress, such as long, exhausting exercise.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 5-9 g a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada ties these uses to periods of physical stress such as prolonged, exhausting exercise.

supported_wordings.wording: Helps support immune health after periods of physical stress.
supported_wordings.why: Health Canada lists it at 5-9 g a day; no other listed source covers it.
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older. Health Canada ties these uses to periods of physical stress such as prolonged, exhausting exercise.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Heals IBS, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names diseases; Health Canada's wording is about digestive health after physical stress.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Protects you from getting sick after training
wordings_to_avoid.why: Implies protection against infection; the supported wording is immune health after physical stress.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
